description: A stereo plate reverb with two pitch shifters in its feedback loop, so the tail drifts away from the pitch of what went in. There is no room size control: the length of the tail is set by DECAY

params.text: Balances the incoming signal against the early reflections, which are two eight tap fractional delay lines with sixteen different times
Delays the signal before it reaches the tank, 0 to 400ms
Balances the signal reaching the predelay against the delayed signal it produces
Sets the pitch shift of the first shifter in the feedback loop, over a smaller range and a smoother curve than the second one
Sets the pitch shift of the second shifter in the feedback loop, over a wider range than the first one
Balances the unshifted signal against the output of the first shifter
Balances the unshifted signal against the output of the second shifter
Sets the highest frequency passed into the reverb
Sets the length of the tail, by setting how much of the tank is fed back into itself
Balances the input against the reverb at the outputs
Scales the signal at the outputs, 0 to 2.0
Holds the tank with its decay set to infinite, so what is in the reverb repeats without fading

inputs.text: The left input of the reverb
The right input of the reverb
A voltage added to the shift set by DISSONANCE1
A voltage added to the shift set by DISSONANCE2
A voltage added to the balance set by DISS 1 MIX
A voltage added to the balance set by DISS 2 MIX
A voltage added to the bandwidth set by BANDWIDTH
A voltage added to the decay set by DECAY
A voltage added to the balance set by DRY-WET
A voltage added to the gain set by BOOST
Freezes the tank from a patched signal, holding its decay at infinite

outputs.text: The left output of the reverb
The right output of the reverb
